title: Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary: Including Novated Lease Salary Sacrifice Considerations
description: Use our hourly to annual pay calculator to convert your wage, understand tax and super, and see how a novated lease salary sacrifice might affect your take-home pay.
salarySummary: Annual pay is calculated as hourly rate × hours per week × 52, assuming a standard 38-hour week for full-time workers.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

faqs.q: Does the calculator include tax and superannuation?
faqs.a: Yes, it estimates tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy (2% for most people). Superannuation is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of your gross pay, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. The calculator does not deduct HELP loans, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging arrangements such as a novated lease salary sacrifice.

faqs.q: What is a novated lease salary sacrifice and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: A novated lease salary sacrifice is an arrangement where your employer deducts lease payments for a car from your pre-tax salary, reducing your taxable income. This can lower the tax you pay, but it also reduces your super guarantee contributions because super is based on your ordinary time earnings after the sacrifice. Our calculator does not account for salary sacrifice, so you should adjust your hourly rate or annual figure manually to reflect the reduction.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Hourly to Annual Conversion

When you have an hourly rate or a salary offer, the first step is to convert it to an annual figure. The standard formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For most full-time roles, we assume a 38-hour week, as set by the Fair Work Commission for the National Employment Standards. This gives you a gross annual pay before any deductions.

For example, if you earn $30 per hour and work 38 hours each week, your annual gross pay is $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. If you work a different number of hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. The same formula works for part-time or casual workers, but remember that casual employees typically receive a 25% loading on top of their base rate.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual employees covered by the minimum wage receive $33.05 per hour, which includes the 25% casual loading. However, many industries have award rates that are higher than the minimum. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) that list the minimum pay rates for your award. These rates vary by classification and industry, so always check the correct award for your job.

### Differences in Ordinary-Time Earnings

Not all jobs pay the same. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) for full-time adult ordinary time earnings at $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). This is a national average across all industries and occupations. For all employees (including part-time), the average total earnings are $1,579.20 per week. These are averages, not medians for a specific job. Your actual pay may be higher or lower depending on your industry, location, and experience.

If you are comparing a salary offer to your current hourly rate, remember that the ABS figures are averages, not the median for your particular role. Use our [reference tables](/data) to see typical pay ranges for different occupations.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a 38-hour week at $30 per hour, your weekly pay is $1,140, so your fortnightly gross is $2,280. This can help you budget and compare with salary offers that are quoted annually or monthly.

### Tax and Superannuation

Your annual gross pay is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) applies progressive tax rates for residents in 2026–27:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

Most people also pay a 2% Medicare levy, unless they qualify for a reduction or exemption. Our calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here. The tax estimate is for a resident with the full tax-free threshold. It does not include HELP loans, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (the super guarantee rate). This is not deducted from your gross pay; your employer adds it separately. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year, so super is capped at 12% of that amount. For example, if your annual gross is $80,000, your employer contributes $9,600 in super. You can see how this affects your total remuneration on our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

### Casual Loading and Ordinary Hours

If you are a casual employee, your hourly rate usually includes a 25% loading in lieu of paid leave. When using our [the timesheet](/) calculator, enter your base hourly rate (without the loading) and check the casual loading box. The calculator will add 25% on top. Do not enter a rate that already includes the loading. This ensures the annual estimate is correct.

### Novated Lease Salary Sacrifice

A novated lease salary sacrifice is an arrangement where you sacrifice part of your pre-tax salary to pay for a car lease. This reduces your taxable income, which can lower the tax you pay. However, it also reduces your super guarantee contributions because super is based on your ordinary time earnings after the sacrifice. Our calculator does not account for salary sacrifice, so you need to adjust your hourly rate or annual figure manually. For example, if you sacrifice $10,000 per year goes to a novated lease, your taxable income for the year is reduced by that amount. This is a common way to manage your tax, but it affects your take-home pay and super. See our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for more on how deductions change your net income.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is an estimate. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more detailed information on your specific situation, refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman, the Fair Work Commission, the Australian Bureau of Statistics, and the Australian Taxation Office. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) and [job pay](/topics/job-pay] pages for more on how to apply these figures to your job.
